explain.say: Each hair grows from a tiny pocket in the skin called a follicle. At the bottom, in the hair bulb, colour-making cells called melanocytes squirt pigment, called melanin, into the growing hair.

explain.say: Different mixes of two kinds of melanin make black, brown, blonde and red hair. Without melanin, a hair has no colour of its own and looks white.

explain.say: With age, these stem cells run low or get stuck, so new hairs grow in without melanin. A mix of white and coloured hairs looks grey. Your genes largely decide when it starts.

faq.a: Hair colour comes from melanin made by cells called melanocytes in the hair bulb. Dark eumelanin gives brown and black shades, and reddish pheomelanin gives red and ginger tones.
asks: Why do people have different hair colours?

faq.q: What happens in the hair bulb?
faq.a: The hair bulb at the base of the follicle is where cells divide to build the hair. Melanocytes there pass melanin into these cells, colouring the hair as it grows.
Pigment stem cells in each follicle gradually run out or stop working properly, so new hairs grow without melanin. White hairs mixed with coloured ones give a grey look.
asks: Why do people get grey hair?

faq.a: Research in mice found that intense stress can use up pigment stem cells and cause greying. In people, stress may speed greying a little, but genes and age are the main causes, and hair cannot turn white overnight.

faq.q: When do people start going grey?
faq.a: It varies a lot and mostly depends on genes. Many people notice the first grey hairs in their thirties, though some start earlier and others much later.
asks: At what age does hair go grey?

facts: Hair colour comes from two kinds of melanin: eumelanin and pheomelanin.
Grey hair is a mixture of pigmented and unpigmented, white hairs.
